question: On 31 January 2024, the College of Commissioners appointed German MEP Markus Pieper (EPP/CDU) as the EU’s new SME Envoy. Due to the controversy surrounding his appointment, after he allegedly scored significantly worse in tests than two female competitors from under-represented Member States, Mr Pieper announced he would not be taking up the position the day before he was supposed to start.1 Given the importance of the SME Envoy, it is now essential to fill the post in a timely, transparent and adequate manner. 1.
How and when will the Commission resume the process of nominating a new SME Envoy following Mr Pieper’s withdrawal?

If the selection is not made from the two other previous final candidates, what assurances can the Commission give that their test scores will have been sufficiently taken into account when filling the role of SME Envoy?

What actions will the Commission take to improve the transparency and accountability of future recruitment procedures as regards high-ranking posts, including, if any, measures to prevent party politics influencing such procedures?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.3.2025) The College Decision of 31 January 2024 appointing Mr Pieper put an end to the selection procedure for the EU SME (small and medium-sized enterprises) Envoy.

Following the withdrawal of Mr Pieper from the recruitment procedure before his contract came into effect, the post of EU SME Envoy remains vacant and no decision has yet been taken concerning its possible republication.

Unless otherwise specified in the vacancy notice for a post, selection procedures for senior officials aim to select a person for a particular post and not to create a reserve list from which the Commission could recruit during a given period of time.

Since the successful candidate withdrew after the appointment, which put an end to the selection procedure, it is not now possible to select any of the other candidates, as the selection procedure is closed. The Commission reiterates that the selection procedure for the EU SME Envoy was run in accordance with the established rules.
